classes.name: GLP-1-based anti-obesity medications
classes.description: Injectable or oral GLP-1/GIP agents labeled for chronic weight management (NOT their diabetes-labeled versions): semaglutide (Wegovy, including Wegovy tablets), tirzepatide (Zepbound), liraglutide (Saxenda). Many plans exclude weight-loss drugs entirely; an exclusion is a valid finding (outcome nonformulary).
classes.plainDescription: A weekly shot (or daily pill) for weight loss, like Wegovy or Zepbound.

classes.name: Oral anti-obesity medications
classes.description: Oral anti-obesity agents: phentermine (Adipex-P, Lomaira), phentermine/topiramate ER (Qsymia), naltrexone/bupropion ER (Contrave), orlistat (Xenical). Many plans exclude weight-loss drugs; an exclusion is a valid finding (outcome nonformulary).
classes.plainDescription: A pill for weight loss, like phentermine or Contrave.

records.preferredRestriction: Not covered for weight reduction without obstructive sleep apnea (reference tool p. 15, footnote ^). Zepbound is preferred with clinical criteria (CC) for its OSA with obesity indication only. No chronic weight-management indication is covered.
records.tier: Not covered for weight reduction (Zepbound preferred with clinical criteria for OSA with obesity only)

paRequired.reason: Non-covered for weight reduction (page 15, footnote #); covered via PA only for cardiovascular and MASH indications

records.verificationNote: Read ref PDL p.15 (07/01/2026) footnotes ^ (Zepbound) and # (Wegovy), and thera PDL p.1 and p.2 (04/01/2026). The document states weight-reduction coverage is excluded for Wegovy and Zepbound, so this is a documented exclusion, not an inference. Wegovy tablets, Saxenda (liraglutide weight) and generic semaglutide are not listed. Diabetes-labeled Ozempic, Mounjaro, Rybelsus, Victoza and Trulicity are preferred with clinical criteria for diabetes and are NOT counted as weight-loss coverage. Marked partial because Saxenda and Wegovy tablets are absent from the document. Confirm with plan before relying on this cell. [Sonnet check 2026-10-21: preferredAgent.inn set to the weight-management label; PA-required wording removed per CC legend finding (the earlier claim that CC agents also need PA is not stated in the PDL legend ('cc: preferred with clinical criteria in place'); the CC agents sit under the 'NO PA REQUIRED' header, so the PA-required wording was removed and the restriction reworded to criteria-in-place. Thera PDL text cited earlier was not re-checked (not in local sources).)]

records.preferredRestriction: No oral weight-loss agent appears in the AL PDL documents reviewed (phentermine, phentermine/topiramate, naltrexone/bupropion, orlistat not listed). Coverage not confirmed; confirm with DMAS or plan.
records.verificationNote: Searched ref PDL (07/01/2026) and thera PDL (04/01/2026) full text: none of phentermine, Adipex-P, Lomaira, Qsymia, Contrave, naltrexone or orlistat appears. The documents do not state that oral weight-loss drugs are excluded, and the PDL says it is not a complete list, so absence is recorded as not confirmed rather than nonformulary. Phentermine is used as the class reference only; it is not presented as covered.

records.preferredRestriction: No weight-loss GLP-1 (Wegovy, Zepbound, Saxenda) appears on this plan's September 2026 list; coverage likely excluded (confirm with plan)
records.verificationNote: Read the whole PDF text layer. No weight-management GLP-1 appears: Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda are absent. Diabetes-labeled GLP-1s are listed as Tier 2 with PA (Ozempic, Rybelsus, Mounjaro on PDF p. 38-39; Trulicity p. 39; Xultophy p. 40); they are not the weight-management indication and are excluded from this class. Web search for a BCBS Alabama 2026 weight-loss exclusion found only secondary sources (none confirmed Alabama), so none is cited. Sig and strength are standard label dosing.

records.verificationNote: Searched PDF text for Wegovy, Zepbound, Saxenda, semaglutide, liraglutide, tirzepatide, and the generic molecules. Only diabetes-labeled Mounjaro (tirzepatide, PDF p. 47), Ozempic and Rybelsus (semaglutide, PDF p. 49) appear, all Tier 3 with PA and QL. None is labeled for chronic weight management, so none is listed as a covered weight-loss agent. The document does not state it is the complete list and tells members to ask Member Services about drugs not included, so this is recorded as noCoveredAgent with partial verification, not as an exclusion. The document does not state a Part D weight-loss exclusion.
